name: Medullary Index Calculator
seoDesc: The medullary index is the width of the medulla inside a hair shaft divided by the width of the whole shaft. Free medullary index calculator: enter your value
summary:
The medullary index is the width of the medulla inside a hair shaft divided by the width of the whole shaft. It returns medullary index, medullary index, medulla diameter and hair shaft diameter, and the panel shows all of them at once.

Forensic hair examiners use it to tell human hair from animal hair: human medullae are thin, animal medullae are usually thick. The arithmetic keeps full precision internally and only rounds what it displays, so the number you copy out is the number the formula produced. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Medullary Index
sections.html:
Medullary index = medulla diameter ÷ hair shaft diameter

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
medullawidth of the central medullary columnµm
shafttotal width of the hairµm
indexfraction of the shaft taken by the medulla—

Where the relationship comes from. The one-third cut-off is the classical forensic criterion described by Robertson (Forensic Examination of Hair) and used in standard hair atlases.

sections.title: How do I use the Medullary Index?
sections.html:
Fill the boxes you have numbers for; the calculator decides what it can derive from them.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Substituting them into the formula gives medullary index of 0.1143, medullary index of 11.43%, medulla diameter of 8 µm, hair shaft diameter of 70 µm.

An 8 µm medulla in a 70 µm shaft gives 0.11 — well inside the human range; the same medulla in a 20 µm shaft would already read as animal-like.

Because the example uses the defaults, you can reproduce it by loading the page and reading the results panel before touching anything.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
Interpretation is a convention, not part of the arithmetic. The usual bands are:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
below 0.33Human-typethin or fragmented medulla — the usual human pattern
0.33 – 0.50Overlappingseen in both, so not diagnostic on its own
above 0.50Animal-typethick medulla, typical of most non-human mammals

  • The conventional cut-off is one third: an index below 0.33 is described as human-like, above 0.50 as animal-like, and the middle band is where the measure stops being decisive.

  • Medullation varies along a single hair and between hairs from the same head, so examiners measure several and report a range.

  • A medullary index is a screening observation, not an identification — microscopic hair comparison cannot individualise a sample.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
Before blaming the formula, check these — they explain nearly every mismatch:

  • Measuring where the medulla is fragmented or absent and calling it thin.
  • Using a shaft width taken at the root, which is wider than the rest of the hair.
  • Reporting the index without the magnification and the measurement method.

faq.q: Can this calculator identify an animal species?
faq.a: No. It separates the human pattern from the general mammalian one. Species level identification needs microscopic comparison with a reference collection or DNA.

faq.q: Why is human hair medullated so thinly?
faq.a: The human medulla is often discontinuous or absent; when present it occupies a much smaller fraction of the shaft than in most other mammals.

faq.q: What does the Medullary Index actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns medullary index, medullary index, medulla diameter and hair shaft diameter. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
